newsitem.title: USA: Florida governor vetoes tax breaks for businesses.
newsitem.headline: Florida governor vetoes tax breaks for businesses.

text.p: Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles has vetoed a package of sales tax breaks for businesses.
Lobbyists had estimated the value of the tax package at $22 million but Chiles put the figure at $30.6 million.

The package was adopted in the closing hours of the Legislature and included a broad range of full or partial sales tax exemptions for transactions ranging from the sale of airplane parts and farm equipment to school bake sales.
The bill would also have granted tax breaks to companies that add more than 1,000 new jobs in urban areas and companies working on research and development projects with state universities.

Chiles vetoed the bill Friday, saying the state needed the sales tax revenues to help provide basic services. He called the bill a classic "tax train," a bundle of unrelated bills hastily rolled together into a single bill.
